content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to CAPM Certification in Lexington

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: Verify you hold a secondary degree and have completed the required project management education hours. CAPM requires no prior work experience, making it ideal for Lexington professionals entering or transitioning into project management roles.

steps_items.heading: Complete 23 Contact Hours of Education
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led boot camp. Our intensive format compresses the required project management coursework into an accelerated schedule, allowing you to meet PMI's education requirement while maintaining your work commitments.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: Complete your official PMI application, providing documentation of your secondary degree and course completion. Submit the required exam fee directly to PMI to activate your eligibility window for the CAPM exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources to reinforce core concepts and testing strategies. Schedule your CAPM exam through PMI's testing partner when you feel confident, then sit for the computer-based assessment.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your Credential
steps_items.text: After earning your CAPM, commit to earning professional development units during the three-year renewal cycle. Granite PM Academy offers continuing education options to help you maintain active credential status and advance your project management expertise.

fq_items.question: Do I need project management experience to take the CAPM?
fq_items.answer: No prior PM experience is required. The CAPM only requires secondary education (high school diploma or equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education — which our course fulfills.

fq_items.question: Is the CAPM a good starting credential for {city} professionals?
fq_items.answer: Yes. The CAPM is one of the most recognized entry-level PM credentials and is highly regarded across industries in {city_state}. It demonstrates PM knowledge to employers even before you have years of experience.

fq_items.question: How does the CAPM differ from the PMP?
fq_items.answer: The PMP requires 36–60 months of project leadership experience; the CAPM does not. Many professionals earn the CAPM early in their career, gain experience, then pursue the PMP.

fq_items.question: Is this training delivered online?
fq_items.answer: Yes. Our CAPM training is fully live-virtual — no travel required. {city} students attend via video conference from wherever they are.

fq_items.question: Is CAPM certification worth pursuing for Lexington project management careers?
fq_items.answer: Yes, especially if you're entering project management or transitioning into the field. Lexington's healthcare systems, manufacturers, and IT service providers increasingly list PMP as preferred or required; CAPM positions you competitively for advancement toward PMP while demonstrating foundational PM knowledge. Entry-level candidates with CAPM stand out, though industry experience—particularly in healthcare, automotive, or manufacturing—remains the primary lever for stronger offers in Lexington's market.

fq_items.question: Which Lexington employers actively hire certified project managers?
fq_items.answer: UK HealthCare, Baptist Health Lexington, and other regional healthcare systems actively seek certified PMs for clinical and operational projects. Automotive and advanced manufacturing employers like Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky and Trane Technologies value certification for quality and production initiatives. Corporate headquarters—Valvoline, Tempur Sealy, and Lexmark—also prioritize certified candidates for cross-functional and IT-driven projects.

fq_items.question: How does Lexington's project manager salary landscape compare regionally?
fq_items.answer: Project manager compensation in Lexington tracks slightly below larger metros like Louisville and Nashville, but remains competitive given the concentration of healthcare, manufacturing, and corporate headquarters. Certified candidates generally position themselves for stronger offers, particularly those with demonstrated experience in healthcare systems, automotive production, or IT service delivery—Lexington's highest-demand PM specialties.
